findings.description: The constructor takes a `const char id[3]` parameter, but this is just syntactic sugar for `const char* id`. If the caller passes a string shorter than 2 characters (e.g., `""` or `"A"`), `strncpy` will copy up to 2 bytes, but if the input is not null-terminated, this can cause reading past the end of the provided buffer.
`strncpy(_id, id, sizeof(_id) - 1);` copies at most 2 bytes, but if `id` is not null-terminated, the destination buffer may not be properly null-terminated.
The constructor does not validate the length or content of `id`. If the input is longer than expected, it will be truncated, which may or may not be acceptable for your application.
Members like `_trigPin`, `_echoPin`, and `_duration` are not initialized in the constructor, which can lead to undefined behavior if they are used before being set.
